notes.title: Hotfix 1.02 🛠️
notes.content:
[h1]🏗️ Good day to you, Constructors[/h1]
[hr][/hr]
A few days ago we published the very first Hotfix to the game, and we’re [b]keeping up the momentum![/b] 🤓 Based on your feedback, we managed to prepare another update in which we are improving several important [b]gameplay elements.[/b]


[h2]A word about controls and camera options[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
However, before we dive into [b]the Hotfix Notes[/b], we want to assure you that we’ve heard your thoughts on[b] control and camera operation issues[/b] loud and clear. We are currently carefully analyzing your feedback and collecting every bit of useful information in order to plan and implement appropriate changes 👷‍♂️ 

[b]Today's Hotfix is ​​the first step[/b] to improve these aspects and make the game even more intuitive and enjoyable. That is why it's [b]full of changes developed based on your requests[/b]. We really hope that you will like all the novelties we have prepared for you!

If you would like to support us in our mission to further improve D&B3, please share your suggestions and ideas on our Discord server, or simply describe your experiences in the comments of this entry. [b]Any input will be greatly appreciated![/b] And now...


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/80472258f0185ed97dff3c621f5b9c0ab5fcee0d.png[/img]


[h2]Hotfix 1.02 Notes:[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
• Adjustments to the mini-excavator arm rotation speed to make them more precise

• The new 3rd person camera system:
- Camera now always turns along with the vehicle
- Fixed jittering 
- Camera no longer goes below ground level
- Smoother zoom operation
- When in operator mode, each attachment has its own camera focus points
- Camera Y axis is no longer inverted by default (requires setting change in the Main Menu)
- Camera is now generally more responsive and intuitive

• When entering the vehicle, the position of the 1st and 3rd person cameras and the driving mode are reset

• The mini-excavator and excavator grappler can now be used to demolish less durable kinds of materials

• The mini-excavator improvements: 
- reduced sliding
- smoother turning
- slightly increased bucket size
- Stiffer vehicle-arm connections (more stability when performing actions)

• Increased turn speed of large excavator

• Changed default key bindings in excavators, the up arrow now raises the arm (requires setting change in the Main Menu - set default)

• Improvements to the controls options: 
- when in options, you will see options of the last used controller
- when in escape-menu, you will see options of the vehicle currently in use
- new shortcuts for better navigation
- new option to assign different inputs to positive and negative axis poles (for ex. right pedal to move forward and left pedal to move backward)

• Hand tools now meet the requirements of assets assigned to a mission before starting it; a section with recommended tools has been added to the mission details window

• Changes to the missions:
- Dig Out Old Wires - the number of cables has been reduced, the ground is now deeper and easier to dig, the cables are now easier to grip
- Demolish a Single Wall - removal of the penalty for damaging furniture, the protective board removed

• Fixed low FPS issue (due to too many messages) when in the laptop screen

• Minor fixes to the physics (collisions between broken fragments, fragments sinking into the ground)


[h2]What's next? 😉[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
As you can see, Hotfix 1.02 introduces many important changes, [b]but our work is still in progress.[/b] In subsequent updates, we have planned to implement improvements such as the option to import additional assets after starting a mission, resetting the player character, and further extensions to the keyboard binding option. More info on this topic coming soon! 

Thank you all, demolishers, for your awesome feedback and factual, useful reports on issues encountered. As always, we [b]remain at your disposal[/b] on our Discord server, Social Media channels and Steam Discussions! More fixes, patches and updates are on their way, so stay tuned 📢

notes.title: Demolisher's Handbook #4 - Controls and Camera Options 🕹️
notes.content:
[h1]🏗️ Hello there, constructors[/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Welcome to the fourth [b](and last pre-release!)[/b] part of our new series, in which we will tell you all about the most interesting, engaging and surprising features of [b]Demolish & Build 3.[/b] You can treat "Demolisher's Handbook" as an introduction to some of the game's mechanics, as well as a helpful guide full of [b]tips and tricks[/b].

Today, we’ll provide detailed answers to your questions regarding the controls and camera options that you will be able to use during your work. [b]Good visibility, precise control of machines and using all possible maneuvers[/b] may prove to be crucial, so put on your hard hats and take notes, builders! You're about to learn some really important skills...

[url=https://discord.gg/HqVqNRr9Uz][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/55e4511ca4fb6bb4e6500148f2825822af225690.png[/img][/url]

[h2]Authentic controls based on real machines 👷[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
The moment you sit at the controls of an excavator, bulldozer or other vehicle, you will immediately notice a [b]set of levers, pedals and buttons [/b]in front of you. Make no mistake - each of them actually serves a purpose and is vital to your future work! 🧐 

Every control element you'll handle in the cockpit of powerful machines is [b]modeled after the realistic, authentic systems found in their real-life counterparts[/b]. Naturally, in order to successfully perform assigned tasks, you must understand and master them all. And although at first glance the whole thing may seem a bit tricky, we are sure you will become proficient in using all the options in no time!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/a3ffd1a5aaeb59dc89f29c1e563a13bd4da2ba63.gif[/img]

Machines and their attachments can be maneuvered in various planes and angles, giving you [b]access to even the most hard-to-reach areas.[/b] Each of the vehicle's tracks can be operated independently of the other ↪️ The excavator arm or bulldozer boom can be freely raised, lowered and rotated, and the attachments themselves can be replaced with others, so it's entirely up to you to choose [b]the right tool for a given task. [/b]

As you can see, the possibilities are almost endless, especially since the mission scenario in no way suggests ready-made solutions, but only assumes [b]a goal that you must achieve[/b]. We can't wait to see if you decide to utilize brute force, exact precision, or some other method! 😁


[h2]Accurate control like never before 📐[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
All the features mentioned above ensure highly accurate and precise control over every part of the vehicle you operate. But hey, there is more! Were you aware that you can easily change the camera angle [b]from inside the cabin to an adjustable outside perspective?[/b] To do so, simply use the "C" key! 

You can also center the view on the attachment mounted to your machine, allowing for even more precise operation. In such a scenario, the [b]camera will follow the arm of your machine and its attachment[/b], for example a saw or bucket. This perspective provides even better control and view of what is happening while performing crucial activities 👀

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/938f41807f4a84333428dc5df266a39233dd9ae1.gif[/img]

Did we mention that some attachments have a [b]built-in camera[/b] that will display the image on the screen in your machine's cockpit? Yeah... camera options are a powerful tool - once you master them, no job will be beyond your reach! 


[h2]Set the controls the way you see fit 🕹️[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Another good news is that you can freely assign [b]any function[/b] (meaning each lever, pedal, button, etc.) to the keys of your choice. The same applies to all types of controllers and joysticks. All elements [b]can therefore be controlled separately[/b] via buttons you assign. How cool is that? 🤩 

Keybinding is one thing, but your options don't end there. During your adventure in Demolish & Build 3, you can configure [b]any number of controllers,[/b] pads, steering wheels, customized handles and other devices, which means you can create various combinations and sets that best suit your needs. Two joysticks and steering wheel pedals? Sure! Pad knobs and keyboard? You got it! There is only one rule - as long as they are recognized by the Windows operating system, [b]you are good to go! [/b]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/7dc92692d2b6a1bba7ca49fe542628b72d4b2166.gif[/img]

Although it may seem like a trick at first, this solution offers a lot of possibilities and [b]ensures authentic, deep immersion.[/b] We encourage you to explore all the options and types of controls until you discover your favorite setup. There's a lot of work ahead of you, so it's important that controlling the machines is clear and simply fun!


[h2]Coming in just 8 days 🥳[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
The big countdown will begin soon, as there are only 8️⃣ days left until [b]Sep 11.[/b] It's like you can already catch the distant rumble of engines and the thud of crumbling walls... the hype is on! As always, we remain at your disposal on our [url=https://discord.gg/HqVqNRr9Uz]Discord server[/url], Social Media channels and Steam Discussions, so take a moment to drop by! 

Be sure to let us know your opinions and suggestions regarding the Controls and Camera systems 💭 Your voices are always very appreciated, as thanks to them, we can better understand your expectations and hopes. notes.title: Demolisher's Handbook #3 - Digging and Soil 🕳️👷
notes.content:
[h1]🏗️ Hello there, constructors[/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Welcome to the third part of our new series, in which we will tell you all about the most interesting, engaging and surprising features of [b]Demolish & Build 3.[/b] You can treat "Demolisher's Handbook" as an introduction to some of the game's mechanics, as well as a helpful guide full of [b]tips and tricks[/b].

And so, it's time to focus on one of the most important activities you will perform during your work as a demolisher and a constructor 🤓 As you know, our title emphasizes the most realistic and genuine simulation of tools, machines, the environment, and... [b]the soil.[/b] In a moment you will see how fun and engaging this seemingly simple element is, along with the numerous opportunities it offers.

[url=https://discord.gg/HqVqNRr9Uz][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/55e4511ca4fb6bb4e6500148f2825822af225690.png[/img][/url]

Let's get straight to work and tackle the tasks assigned by our clients. Today, we're plunging our shovels, excavators, and buckets deep into the ground 🚜 to learn all about[b] Digging and Soil mechanics![/b]


[h2]Everything you need to know about digging 👷[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
In the first part of the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1203670?emclan=103582791471701101&emgid=4327481798743462503]Demolisher's Handbook,[/url] we introduced you to the general physics you'll encounter in Demolish & Build 3, but we mentioned that the digging process is so complex and extended, that it requires a separate entry. You see, [b]every piece of ground[/b] you will set your foot on is carefully simulated and [b]behaves in an authentic, specific way.[/b] This may turn out to be a hindrance... or an opportunity to earn extra money. And this is just the beginning!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/3efda908043db4a3de74a19c84c0f4c31ddad21d.gif[/img]

With the use of mentioned shovels, excavators, buckets and other tools at your disposal, you can dig deep into the ground and, if you feel like it, form a large mound of soil 🏗️ Remember, that earth can be moved, leveled, excavated, relocated and... well, that's just up to your [b]imagination and invention! [/b] Just as with other activities in D&B3, there is never only one path to the goal, and the task itself can be completed in several different ways...

[h3]And here are some of them:[/h3]

[h3]🚧 Digging[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
It might seem like one of the simplest tasks, but digging involves a [b]variety of techniques[/b], each unique in its approach. Some assignments will require you to dig narrow, precise trenches, while others will call for large, deep excavations. 

Digging holes in a quick, efficient and safe (!) way is an art that every constructor must master, as it will often appear on his to-do list. Needless to say, each of them will [b]require different specialized equipment and planning[/b]. Will you be able to stay within the marked lines? Can you go deep enough and choose the right tools? ⬇️ Time will tell!


[h3]🚧 Leveling and shoving[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
Due to the fact that the soil is carefully simulated, it is subject to [b]pushing, moving and leveling[/b]. For example, if there's a massive mound in your way, you can simply push it into a ditch with a bulldozer... if you reach the right speed and tilt the bucket at a right angle, of course! 🤔

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/7d3f99b9625d1480d5a5d3bcc9a5f8fb893c62f2.gif[/img]

This may be a useful skill in cases where a customer asks you to backfill an excavation. Shoving for sure will prove to be much more efficient than moving earth over the hole in [b]the traditional "scoop and pour" way.[/b] Soil can also be moved in other ways, such as with the side wall of a bucket mounted to a giant excavator... although this is cumbersome, it is doable 😅 Once again - it all depends on your needs and preferences.


[h3]🚧 Mounding and piling up[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
The soil you pour out of the bucket will not magically dissolve upon contact with the ground, but instead will begin to form mounds. The same applies to shoving! If your client wishes so, you will need to [b]remove excess soil [/b]from the construction site or level it to a flat surface. It is worth remembering this before starting work in order to allocate the excavated soil wisely.

The formation of sand hills and holes can be tricky, as you may fall into them or get stuck! ⚠️ On the other hand, smart vehicle operation will allow you to drive up such a hill and increase the reach of your excavator's arm. It is said, that an [b]experienced constructor sees opportunities where others see problems [/b]😁 We’re curious to see which one you’ll turn out to be!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/830dcbe6f30953b0cee9400cf38fc8db6a9a6d00.gif[/img]

Now you know that the digging and soil mechanics are definitely more extensive and addictive than it might seem at first glance. But don't worry, we're sure you'll [b]master all the digging-related skills[/b] in no time and prove that no job is beyond your capabilities. [b]Speaking of which...[/b]


[h2]We are just 2 weeks away from the release 🤩[/h2]

We can’t wait for September 11, when [b]D&B3 will be released on Steam[/b], and we hope you're as excited as we are! As always, we remain at your disposal on our [url=https://discord.gg/HqVqNRr9Uz]Discord server[/url], Social Media channels and Steam Discussions.

notes.title: Demolisher's Handbook #2 - Building 🏗️🧱
notes.content:
[h1]🏗️ Hello there, constructors[/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Welcome to the second part of our new series, in which we will tell you all about the most interesting, engaging and surprising features of [b]Demolish & Build 3.[/b] You can treat "Demolisher's Handbook" as an introduction to some of the game's mechanics, as well as a helpful guide full of [b]tips and tricks[/b].

With the first part of our series covering the topic of a [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1203670?emclan=103582791471701101&emgid=4327481798743462503][b]Destruction System[/b][/url] behind us, we can now move on to the next crucial feature. Crushing, ramming, cutting and smashing are a huge part of D&B3's gameplay, but demolition alone is not everything! 😁

You will soon learn, that building skills are just as important... and that is what we will tell you all about in today's Demolisher's Handbook. Grab your hammers, everyone, [b]it's time to build some new awesome structures![/b]

[url=https://discord.gg/HqVqNRr9Uz][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/55e4511ca4fb6bb4e6500148f2825822af225690.png[/img][/url]


[h2]Getting your construction site ready 🧐[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Depending on your client's specifications, you will either build on a clean, empty plot or one where existing buildings need to be removed first. In both cases, [b]thorough preparation of the construction site[/b] is the initial task you will face. An experienced constructor always remembers to take a good look around their surroundings and [b]plan their work wisely![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/f5a6ae5838f5f54274c6bb915c1cccd2dee77086.gif[/img]


When you are sure you are ready to kick off with your work, check out the [b]task list on your smartphone.[/b] Your phone is an extremely useful device, thanks to which you can always check what activity you should do next. And so, [b]since we're talking about the task list[/b], let’s examine the challenges you'll confront on our [b]sample [/b]construction site!


[h2]Step by step - from ground level to the shiny roof 🏛️[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
[h3]🚧 Preparation of the construction site[/h3] - Luckily, we're already done with that!

[h3]🚧 Digging ditches for the frame[/h3] - The next step is quite precise work, because you will have to dig even, often narrow ditches, that will be used during the next activities. May your hand be steady, constructor, as digging narrow trenches requires a lot of accuracy! A vehicle such as the Elevate EXC-12 Compact Excavator will be just perfect for this task.

[h3]🚧 Wooden frames[/h3] - Once the excavator has done its job, it's time to build frames along the excavations. For this purpose, use a hammer 🔨 but before, transport heavy boards with a suitably powerful machine, for example Elevate ES-12 Skidsteer.

[h3]🚧 Concrete pouring[/h3] - Now we will get our hands dirty! When the wooden frames are ready, we need to fill them with concrete. Thanks to this, our building will have a solid foundation and will be much more durable. Unscrew the valves and here we go!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/499adb4a6cbdb0b5841236285cd6d35e3449c682.gif[/img]

[h3]🚧 Floor and wall construction[/h3] - Now that our building has a proper foundation, we can move on to constructing the floor and walls. Special flags with activity symbols will show you which tools you should use to efficiently build them. Depending on the type of building, these may be wooden or brick elements 🧱🌲 Remember that external and internal walls are built independently of each other and are separate fragments of the whole construction.

[h3]🚧 Ceiling and roof[/h3] - The culmination of our work will be the construction of a ceiling and then a roof. Thanks to them, our building will become a cozy, safe place, protected against wind, rain and other weather conditions that our client may encounter in the future. At this stage, a ladder would come in handy—let's hope you're comfortable working at heights! 😁


[h2]Sounds like a plan! 🤓[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Of course, every construction site you set foot on will be different from the previous one, and the construction process itself may be different from what you've seen before. Well, the job of a builder is [b]very varied and full of surprises![/b] It's entirely up to you what tools and machines you use and how you approach the next construction order, as you are your own boss. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/7351c0e26274db2b22ed278020973c2ec691f98a.gif[/img]

What's more, after construction tasks are completed, there may be [b]unused materials left on the site[/b] that will still be of value to your customers. They may ask you to store them in a designated place... for an additional fee! Such bonus tasks often appear among varied orders, so keep your eyes peeled for potential additional earnings 🤑

The money you earn in this way can be used to develop your vehicle park, which over time will be filled with shiny machines, tools and attachments! Sounds like every [b]demolition company owner's dream[/b], right? Every day is a new opportunity!

We hope you are as excited as we are and are looking forward to [b]September 11, when D&B3 will be released on Steam.[/b] As always, we remain at your disposal on our [url=https://discord.gg/HqVqNRr9Uz]Discord server[/url], Social Media channels and Steam Discussions.

notes.title: Demolisher's Handbook #1 - Physics of Destruction 🤯🤯
notes.content:
[h1]🏗️ Hello there, constructors[/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Welcome to the first part of our new series, in which we will tell you all about the most interesting, engaging and surprising features of [b]Demolish & Build 3.[/b] You can treat "Demolisher's Handbook" as an introduction to some of the game's mechanics, as well as a helpful guide full of [b]tips and tricks[/b].

As our first topic in the series, we will discuss something that, in our opinion, significantly distinguishes D&B3 from other titles of this type. Thanks to a completely new, extensive [b]Physics System[/b] 🧐 as this is what we will be talking about, you will feel as if you were[b] really[/b] on an authentic construction site! How so? Let's dive right into it! 


[h2]Every brick, beam and tile matter! 🧱[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Welcome to a world where [b]every single element is physically simulated.[/b] Whether you are breaking small roof tiles, sawing double doors of a shed, or breaking down huge walls of mighty buildings, each of their building blocks is carefully simulated. And these aren't just cool-sounding slogans - there are really [b]immersive and engaging mechanics[/b] to support them! Here's how it works.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/bc977be7503f504ded27b6403c09219d0d0acb0a.gif[/img]


[h3]New Physics in details[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
🚧 Each place and building you demolish is made up of[b] strategically placed pieces[/b]. These can be beams, columns, walls, roofs, doors, rubble, sand piles and similar parts.

🚧 Structures crumble or break in the [b]exact spot[/b] you are working on. You hit the base of the column supporting the building? If the weight resting on it was large enough, you can expect a part or even a whole thing to [b]collapse![/b]

🚧 This means that [b]falling elements can hurt you![/b] Be careful... and if necessary, go to the first aid kit located on your pickup truck.

🚧 Whether you use hand tools or powerful vehicles, their [b]every action and contact[/b] with buildings, ground and debris will matter and have its effect.

🚧 Speaking of which... [b]every vehicle has its own properties[/b], power, weight and physics. For example, you can move smaller vehicles with larger ones (yes, [b]you can lift a mini-excavator with a crane[/b] and strategically place it on the top floor of a building for more precise work), turn them over or push them aside!

🚧 Different [b]materials[/b] also [b]vary in properties[/b] and tool compatibility. A saw excels at cutting wood, while concrete is most effectively demolished with a crusher or jackhammer. We are sure you get the idea!

🚧 With all this in mind, be sure to try out [b]all the possible combinations[/b] of vehicles and their attachments. You'll be surprised how many different ways you can [b]approach the different problems[/b] you encounter!


[h2]The options are almost infinite 🤓[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Sounds really cool, doesn't it? Such an advanced Physics System [b]means a lot of possibilities[/b] and options... but at the same time [b]it can be a hindrance[/b]! 😱 For example, if you are not careful enough, the tracks of your vehicles may get stuck on crushed elements. The roof may fall on your head. The machine may fall into a previously dug hole... However, it's nothing that an [b]experienced Demolisher like you[/b] couldn't handle, right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/1ea7410958ed23d55de84f846a3517694308b7ca.gif[/img]

More examples? [b]You got it! [/b]To crush walls, you do not have to use only hand or pneumatic hammers intended for this purpose. A sufficiently fast-moving vehicle should also be able to cope with them, even if it is currently equipped with a bucket 💥 There is never only one way out, and a lot depends on your [b]ingenuity and creativity![/b] If we add the fact that the arms, attachments and tracks of each machine can be moved independently of each other, [b]we get a truly explosive mixture[/b]!


[h2]The physics of sand and rubble 🚜[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Although we mentioned it above, it is worth noting mentioning it again. In Demolish & Builders 3, [b]every action you take has its effects[/b], and the crushed, sawed and battered pieces remain on the ground as debris. Thanks to high realism, you won't see pieces of the building you just destroyed simply disappearing... what's more, they will stick with you till [b]the very end of your task[/b] 😁 How nice of them!

During your career, you are sure to encounter assignments in which your clients ask you to transport debris to the appropriate containers. [b]Demolishing is a messy job[/b], but sometimes you have to clean the construction site up! 🧹 This is quite a unique feature that sets our design apart and makes the game even more addictive and enjoyable. Remember to always [b]carefully observe your surroundings[/b], avoid getting stuck in debris, and watch out for elements that may fall from above!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42179693/2a9cb3980e3652d231394abfaa8b20740b93ea17.gif[/img]


[h3]Digging holes 🕳️[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
Digging and soil physics are such an extensive topic that we will devote a separate entry to them in the future. For now, suffice it to say that [b]sand behaves just like it does in real life[/b], which means you can dig it up, make piles of it, pour or push it into convenient places [b]and... and more! [/b]More on this coming in the next entries! 


[h2]We hope you enjoyed the first installment of "Demolisher's Handbook" 📙[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
We believe that today's entry helped you understand the principles of the new Physics System and made you look forward to the [b]game's release even more eagerly.[/b]

notes.title: A few words about the little excavator
notes.content:
[h2][b]Fellow demolishers![/b][/h2]

[b]In this devlog we would like to shed some light on one of the vehicles from the game. The compact excavator will be one of your first vehicles in the game. It is also one of the most versatile and will help you on many smaller jobs.[/b]

notes.title: Update demo - full customization for controllers/joysticks/steering wheels
notes.content:
[h1]Demolishers![/h1]

[h3]Many of you have asked for the addition of full optimization for controllers. Especially for you, we have prepared an update related to these changes. As of now, you can assign any function to a button or axis in our [b]demo - Demolish & Build 3: Excavator Playground.[/b]

We took great care to create a system that is both flexible and easy to use. With it you can use any number and any type of controllers. Also, we did our best to allow you to assign whatever button or axis to every important function. In the future we will also add options to calibrate and fine-tune your axes to give you the best experience you can have.
[/h3]

[h3]In the instructions below, we show you how to setup custom controls.[/h3]

⦁	Select your controller here: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/827a46ffeaf897d30902fb68cc6c8d072d11195e.png[/img]

⦁	This button allows you to remove the current assignment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/a50b8412458f37ac25ea56f4e02c87bd8ef6cb33.png[/img]

⦁	To assign a button select a function…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/5ba6272b98a2fd4d1789b7e1c2165b6609b4e260.png[/img]

… and press the chosen button. Only buttons from the selected controller will be pooled. You can also assign an axis as a button (for ex. LT/RT on a controller).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/f7fc7e76c868e7680b4cdd6e7079eeb28060a51e.png[/img]

⦁	To assign an axis, first select chosen function from the list

⦁	There are 4 modes available: Axis, Buttons, Axis with a modifier, Buttons with a modifier

⦁	Axis/Buttons
To assign simply select the function and use chosen axis or button

⦁	Axis/Buttons with Modifier
Axis/Buttons with Modifier is a special function that allows you to use the same controller axis for multiple functions. In practice, the Modifier works like a Shift Key – pressing it will override the default function and use this one instead.

[h2]EXAMPLE:[/h2]

Let’s use this method to setup the Xbox 360 controller to the SAE pattern instead of the default ISO. 
For the sake of this presentation, we’ll use an empty layout but you can just as easily modify an existing one.

⦁	Start by assigning button functions: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/c11052706f1d6ba05d8635245c0e112de53ccd65.png[/img]

⦁	Assign the RT/RB to the right track
⦁	Select [b]right track forward[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/b2b80658989785a47da1ac5f40cef661105ee6e7.png[/img]

⦁	Select [b]no binding[/b] and press RT to assign it 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/7855999a33ed2417cd88f55c3dc13429ffedb58c.png[/img]

⦁	Return to the list

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/35e801d658684a4ec5f4bfa22c670165b2fb5bbe.png[/img]

⦁	Select the [b]right track backward [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/ab63b561cab02788323fd33d39aa21c7169d5b73.png[/img]

⦁	Choose [b]BUTTONS[/b] mode

⦁	Select [b]no binding[/b] next to [b]RIGHT TRACK BACKWARD[/b] + and assign RB

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/8424eb2ee651fef8e4d564d3014202cf064c868c.png[/img]

⦁	Repeat the same for the left track

⦁	Select [b]rotate cabin (left, right)[/b], axis mode, and assign left stick X (horizontal) axis.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/01bc472c24f90a05e9f7283fba39eb84bb9fb11a.png[/img]

⦁	Select rotate boom (up, down), axis mode, and assign left stick Y (vertical) axis.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/67886d36c134266a61b68da0822f113d14ffb970.png[/img]

⦁	Now, let’s move on to the right stick. Select [b]extend attachment[/b], axis mode, and assign right stick X axis. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/3369f479be2945866fca24bdbfa9d2ba4f39f214.png[/img]

⦁	Select [b]rotate arm (up, down)[/b], axis mode, and assign right stick Y axis.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/9c178c0a8dc61d235cd9693a500332afb097e570.png[/img]

⦁	We also need to rotate the shears

⦁	Select [b]rotate attachment horizontally[/b]

⦁	Change mode to [b]BUTTONS[/b]

⦁	Assign D-Pad left/right to the appropriate functions

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/627270aaadc50d6e27e3a8c78c26c53aebd4bae2.png[/img]

⦁	That leaves us with camera controls. Since we’ve already assigned all controller axes we’ll use the modifier.

⦁	Select [b]rotate camera[/b]

⦁	Choose [b]AXIS WITH MODIFIER[/b] mode

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/dc7cf061c25847d3d5864aa93f8086bd25d55dae.png[/img]

⦁	First assign the left stick button to the [b]MODIFIER[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/9432e6e77ac5691775b3e5ad36d1fd618715e2e0.png[/img]

⦁	Now let’s assign the right stick axes to both functions
This means that when we press the right stick button the left stick will control the camera instead of the excavator’s left joystick.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/85e35570d361f55ffc4d12305ac6a0b65bbbf8a2.png[/img]

⦁	Repeat the same steps for [b]camera zoom[/b] with the right stick button and left stick y.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42659669/f937f0a623803e98f607ba263e92b3e3bfe610bb.png[/img]

That’s it. We’ve created working SAE controls for our controller from scratch.


Some additional rules/tips when creating custom control schemes:

⦁	A single axis can be assigned to only one function without modifiers.
⦁	You cannot use the same button for the modifier and a normal function.
⦁	On the other hand, a button can be used as a modifier for multiple functions.
⦁	You do not have to assign every function for a single controller.
⦁	If you want to assign a full axis to one of the tracks, best assign it to the [b]left/right track forward [/b]functions.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1203670

[h3]Stay safe and happy demolition!
Demolish Games crew[/h3]
